# dsh-hint-shell
> **🌐 Language** · English | 中文（简体）
Type `!` in the DeepSeek Harness composer and the rest of the line runs as a shell command, in the w
orking directory of the session you are in.
It is the `!` of a terminal, moved into the chat box: no terminal window, no `bash` tool call of you
r own, and no model request spent on the command.
## Features
- **The composer tells you it is available.** An empty composer gains `, type ! for shell commands`

after the shipped placeholder text, so `!` is discoverable without documenting it separately.
- **Th
e hint appears as you type.** After a bare `!`, a gray `Enter a shell command…` appears right behind

it, and the moment you type real text the hint disappears and gives the line back to you.
- **The o
utput goes into the chat.** `!ls` returns its output as a tool call and result, so the next thing yo

u ask the model about already includes it. **No model request is spent on the `!` line itself.**
- *
*Quoting, pipes, and globs behave as in a terminal.** The command runs through `/bin/sh -c`, or `cmd

.exe` on Windows.
- **One setting.** The command length cap, on the plugin's own row under Installed

.
- **Nothing else changes.** No new button, no replaced component, no altered keyboard behaviour.
## Installation
The repository ships **sources only**: `dist/` is git-ignored build output, so a Git checkout holds
nothing the Harness can load. The installable artifact is the tarball attached to a GitHub Release,
which is already built:
In the Plugin page, choose **Add plugin**, then paste the release asset address for the version you
e Plugin page, choose **Add plugin**, then paste the release asset address for the version you want:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
A downloaded asset works the same way through its local path (`./dsh-hint-shell-<version>.tgz`). Res
tart DSH after it installs.
The same thing from the command line, for scripted setups:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
A Git address also works, because `package.json` builds on install through its `prepare` script:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
That channel needs Node `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0` and a build step, and pnpm blocks build scripts by de
fault: allow the exact key pnpm prints in the profile's `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (`allowBuilds`) and re
-run, or pass `--allow-build` for a one-off install.
To update, repeat the installation with the new release asset. A tarball URL is pinned in the profil
e manifest, so moving between versions means `remove` and `add`. `dsh plugin` forwards to pnpm insid
e the profile directory, so never edit `~/.dsh/profiles/web/node_modules` by hand: the next pnpm ope
ration overwrites it.
## Usage

1. Make sure the composer is empty.
2. Type `!` and keep typing the command, for example `!ls`, or `

!git status`. The hint confirms that the `!` was recognised.
3. Press Enter.
The output is shown in the conversation, and the model can see the command and its result in the nex
in the conversation, and the model can see the command and its result in the next request you send.
## When `!` is a shell prefix and when it is not
`!` is shell intent only when a command follows it on the same line, following the same rule the com
poser already applies to `/`:
| You type | What happens |

| `!ls` | Runs `ls`. |
| `! ls` | Runs `ls`. The space is ignored. |
| `!` alone | Ordinary text, se

nt to the model as prose. |
| `hello !world` | Ordinary text. A `!` in the middle of a sentence is n

as prose. |
| `hello !world` | Ordinary text. A `!` in the middle of a sentence is not a trigger. |
A line that exceeds the command length cap is refused before it runs.
## Limits
A `!` command obeys the same budget as the official `bash` tool, because it is transcribed into an o
rdinary tool call. The plugin reads that budget from the terminal plugin's own settings page at comm
and time, so a timeout you tighten there applies to the next `!` command without a restart:
| Field | Where it comes from |

| `timeoutMs` | the terminal plugin's page (`bash-sandbox`, or `pwsh-sandbox` on Windows) |
| `maxOu

tputBytes` | the same page |
| `maxCommandChars` | this plugin's own setting, default `10_000` chara

cters |
| logged output | capped at `30_000` characters on the way into the session log |
The length cap is the plugin's own because an ordinary tool call has none to inherit: the model writ
es the command into the request, so an unbounded line would be sent twice, once as the argument and
once as the result's echo.
## What the model sees
A `!` result opens with this line:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The wire format does not carry who ran a command, so without it the model would read the record as a
call it made itself. The line is a hint about provenance, not an isolation boundary; it tells the m
odel what happened instead of leaving it to guess.
## Development
Sources are TypeScript; both shipped JavaScript files are generated.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`dist/` is not committed: the build writes only to that git-ignored directory, so a rebuild never di
rties the tree. The shipped bundles come from the release tarball, which the release workflow packs
from a fresh build of the tag.
`test/dsh-format.test.ts` drives the host hook against an installed Harness. It resolves the Harness
packages from the host installation, and reports a skip when none is available.
### Implementation notes
The composer half reuses machinery the shipped composer already has, so the plugin adds no DOM, does
no measurement, and does no positioning:
- **Idle hint.** `LocaleRuntime.prototype.translate` is wrapped, appending one clause to `conversati
on/placeholder.default` and `placeholder.hero`. Every other key passes through untouched, and uninst

alling restores the original method.
- **Armed hint.** The shipped stylesheet already paints this ki
nd of message through `--dsh-composer-hint`. Custom properties inherit, so setting that property on
the composer card is enough for the existing rule to draw the text behind the typed `!`, in the ship

ped caption colour.
